subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: For plain provider messages like `LLM error api_error: Internal server error`, should OpenClaw treat them as cron-local retryable provider outages, shared auth-profile cooldown signals, or timeout-only failures?
rationale: The choice changes provider cooldown blast radius, cron retry timing, and whether operators get early outage notifications, so source inspection cannot safely pick the permanent behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Cron-local provider outage
options.body: Classify plain 500-style cron run errors as retryable provider outages for cron/fallback timing and alerts without marking shared auth-profile cooldown unless the provider signal is structured enough.

options.title: Shared cooldown signal
options.body: Treat plain API internal-server failures as provider cooldown evidence so same-provider candidates and later jobs skip faster, accepting broader suppression risk during ambiguous upstream incidents.

options.title: Timeout-only with proof
options.body: Keep plain 500 text timeout-like only if a focused current-main test proves cron no longer burns the outer wall-clock deadline before retry or alert behavior starts.

recommendation.title: Cron-local provider outage
recommendation.body: Classify plain 500-style cron run errors as retryable provider outages for cron/fallback timing and alerts without marking shared auth-profile cooldown unless the provider signal is structured enough.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-main provenance on the classifier/cron policy lines and prior review context for this decision boundary.
